bug_semantics: File Browser authorized only the requested source root and, for copy or rename, the destination root, then recursively removed, renamed, or copied the whole source tree without checking rules on every descendant. An authenticated restricted user could therefore operate on an allowed parent containing a denied child, exposing or relocating the child at an allowed destination or deleting it with the parent.
flaw_origin: Commit f6816c9a39702484ad7c5c3672209bbc4ce5f948 is the smallest reachable first-writer of the vulnerable resource operation: it created api.go, made serveAPI call c.us.Allowed only on r.URL.Path, routed DELETE to deleteHandler, and had deleteHandler recursively call c.us.fileSystem.RemoveAll on that root. Its immediate parent had no resource delete handler or equivalent user-filesystem recursive deletion. Commit 15f997faf0ff629d8da490c52c023e68a2eb7154 later added rename under the same root-only model, commit 05896697fa2730e59b8bcf6f1253da0f6fb8b5a9 later added copy while retaining only a root rule gate, and b4067cc423b1a0a9d24441bd52e2a53207a49fe9 merely split the already-vulnerable api.go handlers into resource.go rather than originating the flaw.
ai_marker: absent: the raw BIC commit object f6816c9a39702484ad7c5c3672209bbc4ce5f948 names Henrique Dias <hacdias@gmail.com> as both author and committer and contains the subject 'Major changes on API' plus Former-commit-id provenance metadata, with no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI signal.
evidence: The assigned advisory identifies File Browser before v2.63.22 and the unchecked descendants of recursive copy, rename, and delete as the vulnerability, and names 72faf6dd3c85628e332d3e567124b86708ce2695 as the fix. The disputed claims were the primary's b4067cc423b1a0a9d24441bd52e2a53207a49fe9 / f6aeb27ca49647af5b8383fc18c42e3d956f0e7f versus the reviewer's f6816c9a39702484ad7c5c3672209bbc4ce5f948 / d4a43db187d7fb9a2eed650abb89f0011842f93a. `git show --find-renames --find-copies f6816c9a... -- api.go` shows api.go created from /dev/null with one `c.us.Allowed(r.URL.Path)` check, DELETE routing, and `fileSystem.RemoveAll(..., r.URL.Path)`. `git log --all --follow --reverse -S'fileSystem.RemoveAll' -- api.go` starts at f6816c9a. `git cat-file commit f6816c9a...` gives the sole parent d4a43db187d7fb9a2eed650abb89f0011842f93a; `git grep -n -E 'RemoveAll|deleteHandler|resourceHandler|Allowed\(' d4a43db... -- '*.go'` finds only unrelated temporary-download cleanup plus non-mutation rule checks, and a broader parent grep finds no MethodDelete or user-filesystem Remove, Rename, or Copy call. Conversely, `git grep -n -E 'deleteHandler|FileSystem.RemoveAll' f6aeb27c... -- '*.go'` finds api.go's existing deleteHandler and recursive RemoveAll immediately before b4067cc4, while `git show --stat --summary b4067cc4` shows api.go deleted and resource.go created; b4067cc4 is therefore a later handler split/refactor, not a BIC. `git merge-base --is-ancestor f6816c9a... b4067cc4...` succeeds. The BIC is a one-parent direct first-write, not an import, move, or squash aggregate; its Former-commit-id strings are unavailable provenance objects rather than parents or decomposable commits. For the closing boundary, the fix diff adds checkDescendants before delete and patch and walks every source path and mapped destination through CheckRules. v2.63.21 resolves to f6fb8f6bf52d714b2215534033a3c96316069efc and has no checkDescendants; v2.63.22 resolves to afeb478ee1b9d6800d438891d7d56e69204b81f4 and contains both call sites and the walk. `git merge-base --is-ancestor 72faf6dd... v2.63.22` succeeds and the same command for v2.63.21 fails; tags containing f6816c9a begin at v1.0.0. Finally, `git cat-file commit f6816c9a...` supplies the BIC-only human authorship and no-AI-marker evidence.
reasoning: The reviewer wins both disputed fields. The vulnerability begins when a reachable recursive mutation is authorized only at its root, and f6816c9a directly introduced that invariant violation for delete. Its immediate parent d4a43db1 lacks the resource deletion path, establishing the parent boundary. The primary selected b4067cc4 because that commit created resource.go, but creation of that filename is not creation of the flaw: b4067cc4's parent already has the vulnerable deleteHandler and RemoveAll in api.go, and the commit deletes api.go while splitting its handlers into resource.go. Treating that refactor as the BIC violates the move/refactor exclusion. Later rename and copy additions expand the affected operation set but do not supersede the earliest persistent delete vector. The direct 2026 fix closes the shared mechanism at the documented v2.63.22 boundary by authorizing every traversed source and projected destination path. Attribution is based only on the resolved BIC commit object, which has no AI signal, so the gate-complete verdict is NOT_AI.
